summary.title: 8 Product Hurdles Every Founder Must Clear — This PM-Turned-Founder Shares His Playbooks
summary.one_liner: Learn how PM-turned-founder Ryan Glasgow (Sprig) tackled idea selection, segmentation, early customer validation, MVP scoping, iteration and product/market fit, using outcome-driven innovation.
keywords: sean ellis product market fit survey
takeaways: Use outcome-driven innovation: collect 20-40 customer outcomes and find important but unsatisfied ones as opportunities.
Segment the market narrowly and pick a specific underserved customer group before building.
Validate ideas with cold outreach to people you don't know, and keep early design partners to a small set of target-segment companies.
Scope the MVP to only what you cannot do manually; deliver outcomes through manual work first to validate them.
Ask hard questions in customer calls and distinguish discovering product/market fit from merely validating it.
summary.summary: This First Round Review interview with Ryan Glasgow, founder and CEO of Sprig (formerly UserLeap), is organized as eight hurdles founders face from idea to product/market fit. Glasgow describes using Anthony Ulwick's outcome-driven innovation method to find underserved opportunities, then narrowing to product managers at high-growth and at-scale companies. He recounts cold-emailing prospects, running weekly design-partner feedback sessions, and manually delivering the early product before automating it. The article closes with advice on iterating through tough customer questions and discovering rather than merely validating product/market fit.
